cards.title: Be Supportive of Pregnant Friends
cards.body: You may worry you're not good with babies, but you don't know this child yet. Everyone connects differently with different people.

cards.title: Should You Move for Your Child's School?
cards.body: Relocating closer to family has both benefits and costs. Consider building friendships where you are now before making major changes.

cards.title: Adult Children Moving Back Home
cards.body: Many graduates are returning to live with parents due to economic pressures. Adjusting to this new phase requires patience and updated expectations.

cards.title: Listen When Your Child Asks for Help
cards.body: Resist the urge to solve problems immediately for your children. Letting them struggle builds independence and problem-solving skills they'll need.

cards.title: Free Play and Risk in Childhood
cards.body: Children once played freely with minimal supervision; today parents closely hover. Balancing safety with independence matters for healthy development.

cards.title: Ending Sexual Violence Starts in Childhood
cards.body: Prevention of sexual violence must begin early in child development. Teaching healthy boundaries and respect shapes safer communities.

cards.title: Understanding Your Teen's Therapy-Speak
cards.body: Teens now use therapy language in daily conversation like 'triggering' and 'boundaries.' Parents can learn this vocabulary to better understand their children.

cards.title: Parental Concerns Over Children's Books
cards.body: Some schools are removing children's books from libraries following allegations against authors. Parents and educators face difficult decisions about appropriate content.

cards.title: Child Exploitation by Gangs Rising Sharply
cards.body: Exploitation of young children by gangs has jumped 85% in five years. Even younger children are now being targeted for drug trafficking.

cards.title: Tourette Syndrome Device Helps Boy's Tics
cards.body: A wrist device developed by Nottingham researchers is described as 'life-changing' for reducing tics in children with Tourette syndrome. The breakthrough offers hope for affected families.
